title: Tabletop Canary Roleplay Playbook (working notes)
content:
Purpose and scope:
This is a lightweight playbook for structured tabletop rehearsals that exercise cross-functional canary and A/B rollout scenarios. The emphasis is on roleplay (people as systems), fast feedback loops, and creating repeatable artifacts (scripts, synthetic signals, telemetry queries) so teams can run a 45–90 minute rehearsal before the actual rollout.

Why tabletop?
- Avoids spinning infra for every rehearsal; focuses on decision-making rhythm and communication hygiene.
- Lets product, SRE, SE, data, and CS rehearse tradeoffs (latency vs cost vs quality) without production risk.
- Surface unclear ownership boundaries and ambiguous signals early.

Quick rules for facilitators (runbook owner):
- Keep rehearsal < 90 minutes; aim for 45 minutes for first pass.
- Pre-assign roles 48 hours ahead and share the scenario deck.
- Lock the goal: what are we validating? (e.g., canary rollback triggers, steward playbook, stakeholder comms).
- Timebox each stage; call out decision points.

Core roles and brief responsibilities (roleplay-friendly):
- Steward (oncall/product lead): make go/no-go decisions; execute rollback.
- Ops (SRE): surface infra/latency signals, enforce circuit-breakers.
- Data (DS/ML infra): produce quality/metric deltas, synthetic testcases.
- Product manager: decide user-facing tradeoffs and comms.
- Support/CS rep: craft customer comms and triage plan.
- Observer(s): take notes and capture action items.

Pre-rehearsal checklist (to run 48–24h before):
- Scenario brief published (1–2 pages) with success/failure criteria.
- Telemetry query snippets collected and verified (SLOs, error rates, rerank drift, embedding similarity drift).
- Synthetic inputs & golden traces uploaded to shared folder.
- Slack channel / incident bridge ready and tested.
- List of emergency fallback endpoints and config toggles (model pin, route weight) documented.

Suggested rehearsal agenda (45–90m):
1) 5m — Kickoff: objective, success criteria, known constraints (capacity, budget).
2) 10m — Walkthrough of the canary/A-B plan: cohorts, traffic slices, rollout speed.
3) 25m — Roleplay round 1: normal signals (gradual traffic ramp).
   - Ops reads latency/CPU traces out loud.
   - Data reads quality deltas (per-prompt regressions, hallucination counts).
   - Product reacts and sets acceptance/termination thresholds.
4) 15m — Injected anomalies (pick 1–2): latency spike, quality regression, increased safety classifier hits, upstream DB error.
   - Run through decision tree: alerts, steward call, partial rollback, model fallback.
5) 10–20m — Post-decision: comms, customer impact estimation, next steps.
6) 10m — Retro: what failed in the playbook, signals that were missing, action items.

Three compact scenarios (starter set):
- Scenario A (latency-first): sudden 2x P95 token latency in a single region while errors stay low.
  - Primary questions: is latency transient or load-driven? Do we opt for routing to warm nodes or roll back?
  - Synthetic signal producers: SRE reads a table of p50/p95 CPU, queue length, tail latency per model shard.

- Scenario B (quality drift): automated evals show 6% drop in intent-match for the top 200 prompts. No infra alarms.
  - Primary questions: gate on absolute quality thresholds or user-visible regression counts? Canary weight reduction vs model swap?
  - Data to use: per-prompt diffs, embedding-distance histograms, sample edge-case prompts.

- Scenario C (safety spike): content moderation classifier false-positive rate jumps on a cohort, causing user friction.
  - Primary questions: isolate cohorts, enable human review, pause cohort exposure.

Signal catalog (minimal list to have ready):
- Infra: P95 latency, CPU/GPU utilization, queue depth, pod restart rate.
- Quality: top-200 prompt agreement %, BLEU-ish proxies, token perplexity deltas.
- Safety: classifier rejects per-100k requests, false-positive rate on golden set.
- Cost: tokens/sec and projected spend delta for ramp speed.
- Business: MAU exposed, support ticket rate for cohort.

Example steward decision tree (compressed):
- Alert triggers -> Steward notified (pager/slack) -> Triage by Ops+Data -> If infra-only and < 2x threshold: throttle ramp by 50% and observe for 10m.
- If quality or safety breach (above decided thresholds): pause cohort and revert to previous model version for affected slice.
- If escalation after 20m with no improvement: full rollback and incident postmortem.

Minimal telemetry queries (copy/paste friendly snippets to validate ahead of time):
- ERROR_RATE_5M: SELECT count(*)/sum(requests) FROM errors WHERE ts > now() - 5m GROUP BY model_version
- QUALITY_DELTA: compute aggregate label-match(rate) over top-200 prompt set rolling 1h
- LATENCY_P95: histogram(p95(latency_ms), by region, model_variant)

Communication templates (short):
- Internal alert (steward -> slack #rollout-stewards):
  "[STEWARD ALERT] Canary %s: P95 latency crossed threshold (value=%d ms). Action: throttled ramp to 50%, monitoring 10m. Owner: @ops_oncall."

- External customer note (CS draft):
  "Heads-up: We briefly routed some production requests through an updated model which caused elevated latency for a small percentage of users. We reverted the change and are monitoring; no data loss reported. Will follow up with a timeline."

Post-rehearsal artifacts (must produce):
- Short decision log (who did what and timestamps) — add to the scenario doc.
- Updated telemetry snippet stash (tweak thresholds, add missing queries).
- Action items assigned in JIRA (tag: rollout-rehearsal).
- Retro note with explicit followup owner and ETA.

Common pitfalls we've seen (notes from past runs):
- Too many signals in the deck — people freeze. Keep to 3 prime signals per owner.
- Missing synthetic traces that actually trigger regression detectors. Build a small harness that runs a golden set over candidate model variants before rehearsal.
- Unclear rollback authority — always name a steward and a backup.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Decide canonical storage location for rehearsal artifacts (Confluence vs Drive). (TODO: @Evan to propose by 2024-10-01)
- Should we codify the steward decision tree into an internal console button (auto-throttle)? Pros/cons list needed.
- Run a cross-org pilot with two real rollouts this quarter and measure time-to-decision during rehearsals vs in-prod incidents.

Appendix: quick checklist for a 30m rapid rehearsal (sprint-friendly)
- 5m: objective + roles check
- 10m: normal rollout walkthrough (stepped ramp)
- 10m: single injected anomaly (steer to decision)
- 5m: retro + assignments

Notes to self (stream-of-consciousness):
- keep this doc lean; create a folder with scenario templates (one-page), stub telemetry queries, and a short video of a 45m recorded rehearsal for onboarding.
- capture at least two real incidents where tabletop would have changed the outcome; use them as canonical scenarios.

References and inspiration: internal rollout playbooks, incident runbooks, SRE tabletop guides, RLW-1423 (pilot canary automation).
